display.purpose: Game moments only: title plate, combat resolution, elimination, victory, map cartouches. Never UI labels, buttons, or data (the Cartouche Rule). Self-hosted static 400/600.

body.purpose: The working face: UI text, labels, prose. The default face; the serif and mono are opt-in. Self-hosted static 400/600.

label.purpose: Numbers, seeds, odds, telemetry — via the .mono utility with tabular-nums, the honest-tension face. Self-hosted static 400/600.

shadows.name: material-layering
shadows.purpose: The system's ONLY elevation cue, and it is not a shadow: a walnut-800 panel one material step up from the walnut-900 body, separated by a walnut-700 hairline. The Material-Layering Rule forbids drop shadows — if a panel floats, it's off the table. No cool-gray SaaS card-shadows exist anywhere; the one warm exception (victory's title glow) is an animated text-shadow carried in motion, not a resting elevation.

motion.name: duration-fast
motion.purpose: Snappy state change — hover, press, small toggles.

motion.name: duration-base
motion.purpose: Default feedback — selection, composer open/close, tooltip.

motion.name: duration-slow
motion.purpose: Deliberate feedback — panel/rail slide, larger reveals.

motion.name: ease-standard
motion.purpose: Symmetric ease for in-place state changes.

motion.name: choreo-ease-quint
motion.purpose: Ease-out quint — the confident set-piece curve for the elimination sink, the winner/seat staggers, and the victory title glow. Distinct from the feedback easing scale (motion.ts).

motion.name: choreo-ease-expo
motion.purpose: Ease-out expo — the sharper curve for the two most confident set pieces: the combat settle and the victory rise.

motion.name: combat-settle
motion.purpose: Combat resolving: a crisp confident SETTLE from scale(1.015)/opacity 0.72 to rest — tension letting go. Applied via .combat-reveal-animated.

motion.name: elimination-sink
motion.purpose: A player is out: heavier and slower, a somber downward SINK from translateY(-6px)/opacity 0.62 to rest, no glow. Applied via .elimination-animated.

motion.name: victory-rise
motion.purpose: The game's biggest moment: a confident RISE from translateY(9px)/opacity 0.6 to rest. Applied via .victory-animated.

motion.name: victory-title-glow
motion.purpose: A warm brass stage-light blooming on victory's Cartouche title, then fading (--choreo-warm-glow is brass-500 at 0.4 alpha). A bloom, not a persistent shadow; the text stays legible throughout. This is the system's single warm ambient shadow.

motion.name: victory-winner-stagger
motion.purpose: Coalition winners reveal one after another (translateY(5px)/opacity 0.45 to rest), each [data-testid^="victory-winner-"] keyed by its --i index.

motion.name: turn-order-stagger
motion.purpose: Each drawn seat staggers down the turn-order draw (.turn-order-animated > li) — the quietest set piece, a list rhythm.

motion.name: reduced-motion-floor
motion.purpose: Every set piece renders its honest content unconditionally and adds its -animated class on top; keyframes are transform-led with an opacity floor, so an animation that never fires (a background tab, a headless render) leaves content fully visible. prefersReducedMotion() (motion.ts) gives the matching JS branch. Motion stages the moment; it never gates whether content is visible.

components.name: Chrome Button
components.description: The quiet instrument default for chrome-side actions (e.g. the rail toggle). Square-cornered, hairline-bordered, UA chrome fully reset.
components.css: .ds-chrome-button { background-color: var(--surface-panel, #2f2114); color: var(--text-on-chrome, #e6d8b8); border: 1px solid var(--hairline, #3b2a19); font-family: inherit; font-size: inherit; padding: 0.25em 0.75em; cursor: pointer; } .ds-chrome-button:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--accent, #b78d3c); outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Instruments Button (brass affordance)
components.description: The one button per screen that earns the brass budget — brass text on the panel face, brass-400 glint on hover. Composes .chrome-button + .brass-accent.
components.css: .ds-btn-instruments { background-color: var(--surface-panel, #2f2114); color: var(--accent, #b78d3c); border: 1px solid var(--hairline, #3b2a19); font-family: inherit; font-size: inherit; padding: 0.25em 0.75em; cursor: pointer; } .ds-btn-instruments:hover { color: var(--color-brass-400, #c9a24e); } .ds-btn-instruments:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--accent, #b78d3c); outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Brass Action (filled primary)
components.description: Reserved for the ONE primary game action per screen (Start, Commit) — the filled spend of the brass budget. Reverts to quiet chrome when disabled, so no brass is spent while inert.
components.css: .ds-btn-brass { background-color: var(--accent, #b78d3c); color: var(--color-ink-900, #1a140d); border: 1px solid var(--hairline, #3b2a19); font-family: inherit; font-size: inherit; font-weight: 600; padding: 0.35em 1em; cursor: pointer; } .ds-btn-brass:hover { background-color: var(--color-brass-400, #c9a24e); } .ds-btn-brass:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--color-parchment-100, #e6d8b8); outline-offset: 2px; } .ds-btn-brass:disabled { background-color: var(--surface-panel, #2f2114); color: var(--color-ink-700, #4a3d2c); cursor: not-allowed; }

components.name: Table Panel
components.description: The only container: an instrument laid on the table. Material layering (walnut-800 + hairline on the walnut-900 body), no shadows, no nesting.
components.html:
Resources

Per-player resources, the factory-supply gauge, and the event log land here.
components.css: .ds-table-panel { background-color: var(--surface-panel, #2f2114); color: var(--text-on-chrome, #e6d8b8); border: 1px solid var(--hairline, #3b2a19); padding: 12px 16px; max-width: 36ch; }

components.name: Board Surface
components.description: The map's material — parchment with ink text. Legal ONLY on board surfaces (the Parchment-Belongs-to-the-Board Rule); never an app-chrome tint.
components.html: The aged map — the only parchment object on screen.

components.name: Top Bar
components.description: Slim ≤44px table-surface bar: Cartouche wordmark, turn/phase chip, mono seed readout, the brass Instruments button.
components.html: Industrial JuggernautTurn 12 — Cobalt to moveseed 88410552

components.name: Mono Readout
components.description: The honest-tension face: odds, budgets, seeds, telemetry in tabular mono (the .mono utility). Shown whenever drama is on screen.
components.css: .ds-mono-readout { font-family: var(--font-mono, monospace); font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; font-size: 0.8125rem; color: var(--text-on-chrome, #e6d8b8); background-color: var(--surface-panel, #2f2114); border: 1px solid var(--hairline, #3b2a19); padding: 2px 8px; }

components.name: Player Identity Token
components.description: The triple-encoded player identity (color + shape + pattern) drawn by PlayerShapeIcon. Shown here as cobalt: a square with the ring pattern — the CVD floor-pair exemplar where shape is load-bearing, not decorative. Pattern marks are drawn in ink, over the color fill; the token sits on the parchment board.
components.html: <svg class="ds-player-token" width="48" height="48" viewBox="0 0 48 48" role="img" aria-label="Cobalt player — square with ring pattern"><rect x="11" y="11" width="26" height="26" fill="var(--color-cobalt, #2f6f9f)" stroke="var(--color-cobalt, #2f6f9f)" stroke-width="1"/><circle cx="24" cy="24" r="7" fill="none" stroke="var(--color-ink-900, #1a140d)" stroke-width="1.5"/></svg>

components.name: Contextual Composer
components.description: The action surface beside the board — ONE composer at a time (build/attack/defender/setup/…), resolved from game state. A .table-panel section, a mono RuleLine note (hairline-framed and recessed, never a colored side-stripe), and a role=group grid of real keyboard-reachable hex buttons — the a11y action path (the SVG board only reads/points). Rejected commands teach the rule they broke.
components.html: Build one piece for every two resources you control (rounded down).
components.css: .ds-composer { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 0.75rem; padding: 0.75rem; background-color: var(--surface-panel, #2f2114); color: var(--text-on-chrome, #e6d8b8); border: 1px solid var(--hairline, #3b2a19); } .ds-composer-note { margin: 0; font-family: var(--font-mono, monospace); font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; font-size: 0.8rem; color: var(--color-parchment-300, #d8c39c); border: 1px solid var(--hairline, #3b2a19); background-color: var(--surface-app, #241910); padding: 0.3rem 0.55rem; } .ds-composer-hexes { display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 0.35rem; } .ds-composer-hex { font-family: var(--font-mono, monospace); font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; background-color: var(--surface-panel, #2f2114); color: var(--text-on-chrome, #e6d8b8); border: 1px solid var(--hairline, #3b2a19); padding: 0.25em 0.75em; cursor: pointer; } .ds-composer-hex:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--accent, #b78d3c); outline-offset: 2px; } .ds-composer-hex[aria-disabled="true"] { color: var(--color-ink-700, #4a3d2c); }

components.name: Victory Set Piece
components.description: The terminal, persistent victory moment — a .table-panel with a Cartouche display-serif title (the one place the serif is legal: the Cartouche Rule) that gets the warm brass glow bloom, plus the shape-tagged winner(s) with mono names. Honest content renders unconditionally; the glow has a prefers-reduced-motion off-branch. Winner shown is oxide (player 0 — circle/solid).

narrative.overview:
The interface is a map table: a dark wooden surface where a beautiful aged map lies open, instruments and counters arranged around it, a game in progress between people who know each other. Everything on screen belongs to that scene. The hex board is a parchment-and-ink illustrated map — the hero, glowing at center. The app chrome is the table around it: dark walnut and iron, brass fittings, quiet and warm. Designer tooling (balance knobs, agent telemetry) is part of the same scene — the designer's instruments laid on the table, not a separate software product bolted alongside.

The references are Tony's board-art mockup (repo root: IJ board art ChatGPT 2026-05-17.png), the digital adaptation of Brass: Birmingham, and 19th-century antique atlas plates — engraved cartography, cartouches, coastal hatching, plate borders. The system explicitly rejects all four PRODUCT.md anti-references: mobile-game gloss (Clash of Clans candy buttons, juice popups, reward sparkle), generic SaaS dashboard, grimdark wargame chrome, and retro pixel/8-bit.

The color strategy is Committed: the dark walnut table carries 30–60% of every screen, and the parchment board provides the light. This is deliberately NOT the cream/paper near-white default — parchment exists on screen only as the board's own material, framed by dark chrome.
keyCharacteristics: Committed color: the dark table surface carries 30–60% of the screen; the parchment map provides the light.
The board is the hero; chrome recedes and panels earn their pixels.
Tabletop materiality with digital legibility — state must read faster than the physical board, not just prettier.
Warm, crafted, precise; drama is earned (combat, elimination, victory), never ambient.
Layout is structural-responsive (the right rail collapses below 1100px; below 768px is a check-in tier), never fluid-typography-responsive.

rules.name: The Table Rule
rules.body: The dark walnut/iron surface is the app's body. Panels, nav, and tooling sit on the table, in the table's palette (.table-surface, .table-panel).

rules.name: The Parchment Belongs to the Board Rule
rules.body: Aged parchment is the board's material, not a UI tint. App chrome, panels, cards, and page backgrounds are never near-white warm-tinted "paper" — that is the generic AI default, and here it would also dissolve the board's figure-ground. If a panel looks like parchment, it had better be a map (.board-surface is legal only on board surfaces).

rules.name: The Brass Budget Rule
rules.body: The brass/ember accent appears on at most ~10% of any screen. Its scarcity is what makes selected states and primary actions read instantly.

rules.name: The Cobalt–Violet Shape Rule
rules.body: The brief-committed cobalt and violet collapse to ΔE ≈ 9.4 under deuteranopia — the palette's one inherent floor. For that pair, shape redundancy is load-bearing, not decorative: they carry the two most orientation-distinct hard-edged shapes (square vs triangle) and must never be reassigned to the round-ish shape cluster (circle/pentagon/six-point).

rules.name: The Cartouche Rule
rules.body: The display serif is reserved for game moments — the title plate, combat resolution, elimination, victory, and map cartouches (.cartouche). It never appears in UI labels, buttons, form controls, or data. If a settings panel is set in the display face, it's wrong.

rules.name: The Honest Numbers Rule
rules.body: Combat odds, budgets, seeds, and telemetry are always set in the mono face with tabular-nums (.mono) — the numbers stay legible and honest whenever drama is on screen.

rules.name: The Material-Layering Rule
rules.body: Elevation is a change of material (a lighter walnut + a hairline), never a drop shadow. If a panel floats, it's off the table.

dos: Do keep the hex map the largest, brightest, most crafted object on every play screen.

Do dress designer tooling (balance knobs, telemetry, config) in the same table palette and type system as the game — integrated instruments, per PRODUCT.md's "designer tooling wears the same clothes."

Do encode player identity redundantly — color + shape + pattern, via playerIdentity(id) — and treat the CVD gate (cvd-check.test.ts) as the palette's definition of done; cobalt and violet keep the most shape-distinct markers.
Do give combat, elimination, and victory earned choreography — 150–250ms feedback everywhere else, with prefers-reduced-motion alternatives for all of it.
Do show the real numbers (combat odds, production math) in the mono face whenever drama is on screen — honest tension.
Do reset UA button chrome (.chrome-button) — a raw grey browser button on the walnut table is the "generic" tell.
donts: Don't look like Clash of Clans: no candy-gloss buttons, juice popups, or reward sparkle (PRODUCT.md: "mobile-game gloss").
Don't look like a generic SaaS dashboard: no KPI cards, sidebar-nav-with-gradient-accent scaffolding — especially in the balance tooling (PRODUCT.md: "generic SaaS dashboard").
Don't decorate with grimdark wargame chrome: no ornate metal borders, skulls, or texture overload; the box art's drama stays atmospheric (PRODUCT.md: "grimdark wargame chrome").
Don't use pixel art, CRT effects, or 8-bit styling (PRODUCT.md: "retro pixel/8-bit").
Don't use parchment/cream as an app background tint — see The Parchment Belongs to the Board Rule. Audit test: if a non-board element's background is in the warm near-white band, it's a violation.
Don't set UI labels, buttons, or data in the display serif — see The Cartouche Rule.
Don't float panels on drop shadows — see The Material-Layering Rule.
Don't spend brass on more than ~10% of a screen, or on inactive/decorative elements — see The Brass Budget Rule.
